procedure.description: application of skin substitute graft to the foot, first 25 square centimeters, diabetic foot ulcer

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 15271 (application of skin substitute graft to the foot, first 25 square centimeters, diabetic foot ulcer) with date of service 2026-02-14. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not meet coverage criteria for cellular and tissue-based products for wounds.

criteria.text: Full-thickness diabetic foot ulcer, Wagner grade 1 or 2, present for at least 4 weeks, without exposed bone or tendon, active infection, or osteomyelitis.

At least 4 weeks of standard wound care with documented serial measurements showing less than 50 percent reduction in wound area: sharp debridement, offloading, moist wound dressings, infection control, and glycemic management.
Adequate arterial perfusion documented: ankle-brachial index of 0.7 or greater, toe pressure of 40 mmHg or greater, or transcutaneous oxygen pressure of 30 mmHg or greater.
Hemoglobin A1c of 12 percent or less, an offloading device in place, and tobacco cessation counseling where applicable.

chart.text: Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Vitamin D came back 15. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

78 year old woman with type 2 diabetes for 21 years and peripheral neuropathy, new to the wound center, referred by podiatry. Did not notice the ulcer until her spouse saw blood on the sock. Her history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor, seasonal allergies, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Plantar left forefoot ulcer under the first metatarsal head, present 7 weeks, 3.4 by 2.1 centimeters and 0.3 deep, full thickness into subcutaneous tissue, does not probe to bone, no exposed tendon, Wagner grade 2. No cellulitis, no drainage, no odor. Offloading boot dispensed today, fitted, she agrees to wear it for all weight bearing. Nonsmoker.
Hemoglobin A1c 8.2 percent. Creatinine 1.0. Albumin 3.8.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 224, LDL 157, HDL 61, triglycerides 128. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Left foot three views: no osteomyelitis, no soft tissue gas, no foreign body. Neuropathic changes at the midfoot.
Week 1 of standard care. Sharp debridement to healthy bleeding tissue, collagen dressing, offloading boot worn per patient. 3.4 by 2.1.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Week 2. Sharp debridement, collagen dressing. 3.3 by 2.1. Boot compliance good.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Week 3. Sharp debridement, collagen dressing. 3.2 by 2.0. Slow.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Week 4. 3.2 by 2.0, area 6.4 square centimeters, down from 7.1 at the start, about 10 percent reduction after 4 weeks of standard care with debridement, offloading, and moist dressings. Less than 50 percent; qualifies for a cellular tissue product. Sharp debridement today.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Application of a cellular tissue-based product to the left plantar forefoot ulcer after sharp debridement, 4 square centimeters, secured with a nonadherent dressing and the offloading boot. Weekly follow-up.

expected.note: The chart never addresses crit-3 (perfusion); no entry supports it, so an appeal would assert what the record does not contain.
